html:
Alice Springs is a town in the middle of Australia, in the south of the Northern Territory, on the country of the Arrernte people, who call it Mparntwe.

It began in 1872 as a repeater station on the Overland Telegraph Line, which joined Adelaide to Darwin and so to the cable to Britain. The station took its name from a waterhole named after Alice Todd, the wife of the line's builder, Charles Todd. A small town nearby, at first called Stuart, was renamed Alice Springs in 1933. The railway from Adelaide reached it in 1929.

It grew as the service town of the centre, for cattle stations, missions and later tourists heading to Uluru. The Royal Flying Doctor Service and the School of the Air, which taught children on far stations by radio, worked from it.

Many Aboriginal peoples of the centre live in and around it, among them the Luritja, Anmatyerr, Warlpiri and Kaytetye. West of the town lies Papunya, where the Papunya Tula painting movement began in 1971.
sum: Alice Springs is a town in the middle of Australia, in the south of the Northern Territory, on the country of the Arrernte people, who call it Mparntwe.
